en: to be cancelled; to fail, break down
src: Both examples are the everyday sense — «Der Server war ausgefallen», «Die Heizung ist ausgefallen». „to sortie, to sally" is a military reading that no B1 learner will ever need and that neither example shows.
The examples are both the plural *Mittel* = funds — «Er hat unendliche Mittel», «Tom gehen die Mittel aus». „appliance" is not a sense of Mittel at all.

A false friend left unglossed. German *ambulant* is the medical *outpatient* — which both examples show — while English *ambulant* means able to walk. Glossing it with its own cognate taught the trap instead of the word.
Both examples are «Stress abbauen» = relieve stress, which the gloss did not cover. The dismantling sense is kept because it is the literal one and the synonyms already carry it.
Both examples are «mit uns abhängen» = hang out, a sense the gloss omitted although the card's own synonyms already list herumhängen and rumhängen.
Both examples are «Ich muss abhauen» = I have to leave, and the card's synonyms are davonlaufen / davonmachen. The literal chopping sense is the rarer one and was the only one glossed.

expect.en: to force to leave, to drive away

en: to drive away, expel; to dispel, to pass (the time)
src: Neither example is expulsion: «Heimweh vertreiben» is dispelling homesickness and «sich die Zeit vertreiben» is passing the time. Both senses added rather than replacing, since driving away is genuine.
